Alger, 16 novembre 2026 (Algeria Tech) —: Algiers, November 16, 2026 (Algeria Tech) — The IBM group announced the launch of a fellowship program aimed at educational leaders and teachers in the K-12 sector in the United States, at a time when a survey reveals that a minority of educators have received in-depth training in artificial intelligence.
Formation à l'intelligence artificielle: Artificial intelligence training for educators: IBM unveils a pilot program and poll results
La société IBM a annoncé, le 2 septembre: IBM announced on September 2, 2026, the creation of an artificial intelligence-focused fellowship program for leaders and teachers in the K-12 cycle. This inaugural cohort was slated to bring together up to one hundred superintendents, instructional leaders, and educators from the greater New York area. Participants are required to complete learning and earn certifications through IBM SkillsBuild, described as IBM's free educational program.
En parallèle, une enquête relayée par Te: In parallel, a survey reported by Technical Education Post (at techedmagazine.com) examined the use of AI in the classroom and teacher preparedness. The study surveyed 2,048 American adults, split between 1,019 K-12 education professionals and 1,029 parents. IBM reports a margin of error of ±3 percentage points for each of the two samples.
Selon les résultats de cette étude, 76%: According to the results of this study, 76% of middle school teachers and 73% of high school teachers surveyed report using artificial intelligence every week. In contrast, only 20% of the K-12 educators consulted state that they have received in-depth training in this field.
L'évaluation de pertinence d'ALGERIATECH: ALGERIATECH's relevance assessment specifies that the geographic scope of this American fellowship does not extend to Algeria, although it offers a point of comparison in terms of professional development for Algeria Venture and Algerian teams responsible for teacher training.
